3. The land in question originally belonged to one Sayed Ali who transferred the same to the opposite party Nos. 2 and 3 who subsequently transferred the same to the pre-emptee Md. Ali Ashraf by a registered kabala dated 18.9.02 against which the pre-emptor, A.N.M. Shahidul Islam Bhuiyan filed the Pre-emption Miscellaneous Case being No. 31 of 2004 in the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar, Comilla. Previously the Case was filed under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and subsequently was converted into one under section 24 of the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act wherein the pre-emptor filed an application under Order 39 Rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure for restraining the pre-emptee from proceeding with his on going Residential- cum- Commercial construction thereupon. In the said application it was mentioned that if such construction is made upon the case land by the pre-emptee, the pre-emptor would suffer a colossal financial loss and hence the application for injunction. 

 5. Mr. Anwar Hossain, the learned Advocate appearing for the appellant-petitioner submits that the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar, Comilla was not just in passing the order of injunction dated 23.2.2005 and that the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Comilla too was not just in upholding the aforesaid decision of the Senior Assistant Judge inasmuch as the pre-emptor had nothing to lose when section 24 (3) of the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act is clear that the pre-emptor would be free from encumbrances, if any, what has been spent after the notice of the application has been served upon the pre-emptee. 

 6. Mr. Sarder Abul Hossain, the learned Advocate appearing for the respondent-opposite parties, however, could not controvert the submission of Mr. Anwar Hossain, the learned Advocate for the petitioner in reference to section 24(3) of the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act and we find substance in the submission of the learned Advocate for the Appellant-petitioner as made above. 

 7. In view of the provision of section 24(3) of the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act we are constrained to hold that since the pre-emptor's entitlement and encumbrances on the property under pre-emption is protected under section 24(3) of the Act there was no necessity to pass an order of temporary injunction as has been passed in the instant case. If any construction as alleged has been made upon the case land by the pre-emptee after the notice of the application has been served upon him the responsibility thereof would be borne by the pre-emptee at his own risk and not by the pre-emptor.
